title: Why Don’t Hurricanes Form on the Equator?
description:
The warmest ocean water is there—so why are hurricanes missing?

The Coriolis effect is essentially zero at the equator, so developing storms lack enough planetary spin to organise into a tropical cyclone.

Storms typically need to form at least several degrees of latitude away, along with warm water, moisture and favourable winds.

Cyclones rotate opposite directions in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
